9-1: Despereaux is about to be sent to the dungeon for something he does not think was wrong. Write about a time you got in trouble for something you did not think was bad.
Did I use a capital letter at the start of each sentence?
9-2: The Mouse Council votes, and Despereaux's own father votes with them. If you were Lester, what would you have done? Why?
Did I end each sentence with a period, question mark, or exclamation point?
9-3: Despereaux says one word to the threadmaster instead of saying he is sorry. If you could say one word to the Mouse Council, what would it be?
Did I use a capital letter for every name?
9-4: Despereaux hears a voice in the dark and cannot see who it belongs to. Write about a sound you have heard in the dark. What did you imagine it was?
Did I read my writing out loud to check that it makes sense?
10-1: Roscuro is a rat who loves light, which is strange for a rat. Write about something you love that other people find strange.
Did I use a capital letter at the start of each sentence?
10-2: Roscuro talks to a prisoner who says he did something terrible long ago. Write about a time you had to tell someone the truth about a mistake.
Did I put a comma between the day and the year in any date I wrote?
10-3: Roscuro looks down at the banquet hall and thinks it is the most beautiful thing he has ever seen. Describe the most beautiful place you have ever been.
Did I use describing words that tell what something looked like?
10-4: One small action changes everything for Roscuro. Write about a small thing that once changed a whole day for you.
Did I end each sentence with the right punctuation mark?
11-1: Mig's father sells her, and she watches him walk away. Write about a time you had to say goodbye to someone. How did it feel?
Did I use a capital letter for every name?
11-2: Mig sees the princess for the first time and wants to be her. Write about someone you have wanted to be like. What is it about them?
Did I start each sentence with a capital letter?
11-3: Mig is told she cannot have what she wants, over and over. Write about something you want that is hard to get. What would you do to get it?
Did I circle any word I was not sure how to spell?
11-4: Mig is sent to work in the kitchen because nothing else worked out. Write about a job you have had to do that you did not choose.
Did I read my writing out loud to check that it makes sense?
12-1: Mig is not afraid of the dungeon because she cannot hear it. Write about something that used to scare you but does not anymore.
Did I use a capital letter at the start of each sentence?
12-2: Roscuro makes Mig a promise he does not mean to keep. Write about a promise someone made to you. Did they keep it?
Did I put quotation marks around the words a person said?
12-3: Despereaux dreams about everyone he has lost. Write about a dream you remember. What happened in it?
Did I end each sentence with the right punctuation mark?
12-4: The Princess Pea wakes to find someone standing over her bed with a knife. Write about the scariest moment in a story you have read.
Did I use a capital letter for every name?
13-1: Cook cries about the missing princess even though she pretends not to care. Write about a time you pretended not to care about something.
Did I start each sentence with a capital letter?
13-2: The king loves his daughter with his whole heart but makes ridiculous laws. Can someone be good and wrong at the same time? Write what you think.
Did I read my writing out loud to check that it makes sense?
13-3: Cook breaks the king's law to make soup, and gives some to a mouse. Write about a rule you think should be broken, and why.
Did I circle any word I was not sure how to spell?
13-4: Despereaux is given soup by someone who hates mice. Write about a time someone was kind to you when you did not expect it.
Did I end each sentence with the right punctuation mark?
14-1: Despereaux walks into the dungeon carrying only a needle. Write about a time you did something brave while you were still afraid.
Did I use a capital letter at the start of each sentence?
14-2: Mig is given a crown and told she is a fool in the same breath. Write about a time words hurt more than you expected.
Did I put quotation marks around the words a person said?
14-3: Despereaux holds the needle to Roscuro's heart and then lowers his head. Why do you think he does not use it? Write what you believe.
Did I use commas between the items in a list?
14-4: The story ends with soup, and with almost everyone forgiven. Write about someone you would like to forgive, or ask forgiveness from.
Did I read my writing out loud to check that it makes sense?
15-1: Pick your favourite moment in the whole book and write about why it stayed with you.
Did I start each sentence with a capital letter?
15-2: If you could ask Kate DiCamillo one question about this book, what would it be? Write the question and why you want to know.
Did I end each sentence with the right punctuation mark?
15-3: Choose one character and write three sentences in their voice, as if you were them.
Did I put quotation marks around the words a person said?
15-4: Write the opening of your own story the way this book opens: someone small, in a place that does not want them.
Did I circle any word I was not sure how to spell?
16-1: Despereaux and Roscuro both go looking for light. Write about which of them you understand better, and why.
Did I use a capital letter for every name?
16-2: All three main characters want something they are told they cannot have. Write about which one you would help first.
Did I start each sentence with a capital letter?
16-3: This book says that stories are light. Write about a story that has been light for you.
Did I read my writing out loud to check that it makes sense?

Did I check that my whole letter makes sense from beginning to end?
